title: The Aviary of Falling Feathers
story: High in the Windvane Aviary, Quillowrack the Molting Rook has trapped twelve songbird chicks in a wicker gondola dangling from a fraying rope. The rope is slipping downward toward the thornbriar at a steady 8.5 feet every minute, while Mr 6 cranks the old winch, hauling the gondola back up at 11 feet every minute. The gondola starts 21 feet above the thorns, and Mr 6 must lift it to the safe ledge 18 feet above where it hangs now.
question: If Mr 6 cranks steadily while the rope keeps slipping, how many minutes will it take the gondola to rise the 18 feet to the safe ledge?
solution: Each minute the gondola really gains 11 - 8.5 = 2.5 feet.
To climb 18 feet at 2.5 feet per minute: 18 / 2.5 = 7.2.
Mr 6 needs 7.2 minutes of steady cranking.
praise: Finding the difference between cranking and slipping is exactly the right move — the last step was dividing the 18 feet by that net speed.
hint: The rope pulls down while Mr 6 pulls up. What is the gondola's REAL gain in one minute?
victory: At 7.2 minutes the gondola kissed the ledge and twelve chicks tumbled out cheeping. Quillowrack shed one embarrassed feather and flapped off to molt somewhere less mathematical.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight in a blue cape cranking a wooden winch on a high windy aviary platform at golden hour, a wicker gondola full of tiny chicks rising toward him while a huge sooty rook glares from a rafter.
